memory: I keep: 0.25 mm neoprene eliminates microslip but extrudes ~1.6 N. A 1.5 mm ring raised threshold to ~1.9 N but failed at ring–gasket interface near 1.95–2.0 N. Single central screw creates eccentric preload. New: 3.0 mm ring with ±0.02 mm aperture and two opposite screws raised threshold to ≈2.31 N and preserved near-zero microslip until extrusion. Failure now concentrates at the backing-ring inner lip adjacent to screws. Two screws reduce eccentricity but introduce localized high stress. Current position: need a way to redistribute inner-lip stress without reintroducing microslip.
openQuestion: Does adding a thin 0.5 mm compliant metal spacer at the ring inner lip and using three evenly spaced screws raise extrusion threshold above 2.5 N without microslip?
